title: Lifting Circuit Breaker Measures and Safeguards to Minimise Risk of Second Wave of COVID-19 Infections
what_it_is: Lifting Circuit Breaker Measures and Safeguards to Minimise Risk of Second Wave of COVID-19 Infections

sections.label: Questions on lifting circuit breaker
sections.summary: Questions asked the Minister for Health about lifting circuit breaker measures, lessons from other jurisdictions, and reopening workplaces, sports facilities, malls and food outlets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Health what are the merits of lifting the circuit breaker measures from 1 June 2020 when the rate of infection amongst migrant workers remains in its hundreds and what steps will be taken to ensure that the infection is contained within their residences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Health what lessons can be learnt from other jurisdictions on how to prevent, minimise or manage a second wave of COVID-19 infections as our economy is opened gradually.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Health in view of the low COVID-19 infection rates within our community presently, whether the Ministry will consider (i) allowing all workers and employees whose workplaces meet safe distancing criteria to return to their workstations (ii) re-opening all outdoor sports facilities such as stadiums and swimming pools; and (iii) re-opening all retail malls and food and beverage outlets as long as they can meet safe distancing measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Health whether the Ministry can consider allowing food and beverage outlets to operate for business on 2 June 2020 on the condition that they implement safe distancing among the diners and limit the number of diners per table to a reasonable number.

sections.label: Lessons and cautious Phase One reopening
sections.summary: The Multi-Ministry Task Force takes a cautious, graduated approach in Phase One, resuming low-risk economic activities with safe management measures, as community cases may rise after the circuit breaker.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: The last and most important lesson we have learnt from other countries is that we cannot be complacent as there is always the risk of a second wave of the virus.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We have seen a steady decline in community cases, to four cases per day in the past week.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: But we should be mindful that this is probably the effect of the circuit breaker.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We expect to see a rise in new community cases as the activity levels and person-to-person interactions increase after the circuit breaker.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: The Multi-Ministry Task Force has therefore taken a cautious and graduated approach to ensure safe opening in Phase One.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We have decided to first resume economic activities that do not pose high risk of transmission, such as manufacturing and production operations, and work in office settings which have no or minimal interactions with customers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: To keep workers safe, employers are required to put in place safe management measures such as enabling employees to telecommute where possible, avoiding face-to-face contact meetings and ensuring regular disinfection of common touch points and equipment at work premises.

sections.label: Recovered workers leaving dormitories
sections.summary: Only workers who have recovered or tested negative will be allowed to leave the dormitories.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Only those workers who have recovered or tested negative will be allowed to leave the dormitories.

sections.label: Phase Two resumption of services
sections.summary: Retail, food and beverage dine-in, personal, health and wellness and home-based services resume in Phase Two with safe management measures, and small groups of up to five may meet.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: In response to Mr Chong Kee Hiong and Mr Lim Biow Chuan’s questions, retail, food and beverage dine-in services, as well as personal, health and wellness and home-based services will resume in Phase Two, subject to safe management measures being in place.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Some may start earlier, others may need a bit more time to put in place the necessary safeguards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We will also allow small groups to meet up in Phase Two, including dining together, so long as they do not exceed five persons.

sections.label: Easing towards Phase Three
sections.summary: If community transmissions remain low and well contained, measures will continue to ease until a COVID-safe normal in Phase Three, expected to last until an effective vaccine or treatment is developed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: If community transmissions remain low and well contained, we will continue to ease measures and even increase the pace until we reach a new COVID-safe normal in Phase Three, which we expect to remain in, until an effective vaccine or treatment is developed.

sections.label: Screening migrant workers and reopening economy
sections.summary: Proactive screening of migrant workers in dormitories may take until August or September, and if Phase One remains safe, Phase Two may proceed before the end of the month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: The proactive screening of migrant workers in the dormitories will take some time because we have to do it systematically and carefully.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: They may take up to August or even September.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Therefore, we want to make sure that those who are able start work are safe in the community.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: And therefore, that will allow us to continue the process of opening our economy and if we are safe and remain safe in Phase One, we will then be able to proceed to Phase Two, hopefully – if all goes well – before the end of the month.

sections.label: Phase Two social gatherings opening
sections.summary: It will lead to a general opening of society and community and allow social gatherings of a certain number of people, a consideration for Phase Two.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Therefore, it will lead to a general opening of the society, of the community and allow social gatherings of certain number of people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: This will be a consideration for Phase Two.

sections.label: F&B safe distancing measures
sections.summary: For F&B, measures to ensure safe distancing and minimise mixing must be discussed, and because it involves the public, it must align with community opening in Phase Two.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Similarly, for the F&B, we want to reach out and discuss with them what are the measures that we can put in place to ensure safe distancing and minimise mixing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: But because it involves the public, consumers in the community, it has to be aligned with the opening of the community, which is generally in Phase Two.
